name: MonarchPageOutline
title: PageOutline
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.lazy.LazyColumn of clickable rows with androidx.compose.material3.Text; scrolls itself with LazyListState.animateScrollToItem
summary: A document's headings as a nested list, with the section being read marked as current; picking a heading lets the app scroll to it.
whenToUse: Beside or over a long document, note or help article, usually in a MonarchBottomSheet on phones and in a side pane on tablets, so people can see its structure and jump to a section.
whenNotToUse: For moving between screens, use the app's navigation. For a hierarchy people expand and select, use MonarchTreeView.
api: @Composable fun MonarchPageOutline(headings: List<MonarchPageOutlineHeading>, onNavigate: (MonarchPageOutlineHeading) -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, currentId: String? = null, maxLevel: Int = 3, stats: MonarchPageOutlineStats? = null, enabled: Boolean = true, showTitle: Boolean = true, state: LazyListState = rememberLazyListState(), labels: MonarchPageOutlineLabels = MonarchPageOutlineLabels())
class MonarchPageOutlineHeading(text: String, level: Int, id: String)
class MonarchPageOutlineStats(words: Int, minutes: Int) { companion object { const val WORDS_PER_MINUTE: Int = 220; fun fromText(text: String): MonarchPageOutlineStats } }
class MonarchPageOutlineLabels(title: String? = null, empty: String? = null, stats: ((MonarchPageOutlineStats) -> String)? = null, current: String? = null)

options.name: headings
options.description: The headings in document order, each with its text, level 1 through 6 and the id used to scroll to it.

options.name: onNavigate
options.description: Called when a heading is picked. Scroll the document here, for example with LazyListState.animateScrollToItem, and close the sheet.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the outline. Give it a bounded height: it scrolls on its own.

options.name: currentId
options.description: The id of the heading of the section being read. The app works it out from the document's scroll position.

options.name: stats
options.description: The word count and reading time shown under the list, such as "1,234 words · 6 min read". MonarchPageOutlineStats.fromText counts them.

options.name: showTitle
options.description: Shows the "On this page" title. Hide it when the sheet's title already says it; the outline keeps it as its spoken name.

options.name: state
options.description: The scroll state of the outline's own list.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the title, the empty message, the stats line and the spoken "Current section".

states.name: current
states.description: The current heading is in the accent strong color and the strong body style, with an accent bar at its start.

states.name: other headings
states.description: Muted text with a subtle bar, indented one step per nesting level.

states.name: empty
states.description: "Headings you add appear here." in muted text.

states.name: disabled
states.description: Headings use the disabled text color and cannot be picked.

appearance: No container of its own: the title in the label style, headings in the body style with a 2dp bar at their start, the current one in the accent strong color with an accent strong bar, the others muted with a subtle border-coloured bar. All are theme roles, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: The web outline reads headings from a Tiptap editor or the page and follows the scroll position with an IntersectionObserver. On Android the app passes the headings and the current id, because only the app knows its document and its LazyListState, and scrolls to a heading in onNavigate; this is the same split as iOS. There is no rich text editor on Android yet, so the editor mode and its caret tracking are not offered; MonarchPageOutlineStats.fromText replaces the editor's word count. The outline is a LazyColumn, as the plan says, so it needs a bounded height (a sheet or a pane) and cannot sit inside another vertical scroll; it scrolls itself to keep the current heading in view, which the web does not need. Headings are rows, not links: Android has no link role. The iOS isTitleHidden is showTitle here, following the Android naming of booleans.
accessibility: The outline is a traversal group named by its title ("On this page"); the visible title is a heading.
Each heading is one clickable element with a 48dp minimum height.
The current heading is selected and has the state "Current section", and is shown with a stronger weight and a bar as well as color.
Indentation uses start padding, so nesting mirrors right to left.
Long headings wrap at the largest font size; nothing is truncated.
Scrolling to the current heading is immediate when animations are turned off.
edgeCases: Skipped levels (a level 3 under a level 1) add one step of indent, not two.
Blank headings and headings deeper than maxLevel are left out.
Heading ids are list keys, so they must be unique.
fromText counts at least one minute, even for an empty text.

examples.title: Static headings
examples.template:
MonarchPageOutline(
    headings = headings,
    onNavigate = { heading -> current = heading.id },
    currentId = current,
    labels = MonarchPageOutlineLabels(title = {{title}}),
)
examples.setupTemplate:
var current by remember { mutableStateOf<String?>({{activeId}}) }
val headings = listOf(
    MonarchPageOutlineHeading({{headings.0.text}}, {{headings.0.level}}, {{headings.0.id}}),
    MonarchPageOutlineHeading({{headings.1.text}}, {{headings.1.level}}, {{headings.1.id}}),
    MonarchPageOutlineHeading({{headings.2.text}}, {{headings.2.level}}, {{headings.2.id}}),
    MonarchPageOutlineHeading({{headings.3.text}}, {{headings.3.level}}, {{headings.3.id}}),
    MonarchPageOutlineHeading({{headings.4.text}}, {{headings.4.level}}, {{headings.4.id}}),
)
examples.setup:
var current by remember { mutableStateOf<String?>("accounts") }
val headings = listOf(
    MonarchPageOutlineHeading("Overview", 2, "overview"),
    MonarchPageOutlineHeading("Getting started", 2, "getting-started"),
    MonarchPageOutlineHeading("Accounts", 3, "accounts"),
    MonarchPageOutlineHeading("Permissions", 3, "permissions"),
    MonarchPageOutlineHeading("Billing", 2, "billing"),
)
examples.code:
MonarchPageOutline(
    headings = headings,
    onNavigate = { heading -> current = heading.id },
    currentId = current,
    labels = MonarchPageOutlineLabels(title = "In this document"),
)

examples.title: In a side pane, without the visible title
examples.code:
MonarchPageOutline(
    headings = listOf(
        MonarchPageOutlineHeading("Install", 2, "install"),
        MonarchPageOutlineHeading("Configure", 2, "configure"),
    ),
    onNavigate = { /* scroll to it.id */ },
    modifier = Modifier.height(240.dp),
    currentId = "install",
    showTitle = false,
)
